subject: Energy
title: Moderators and Coolants
description: A 60-second lesson on Moderators and Coolants.

hook.text: Neutrons from fission are too fast—moderators slow them down to increase the chance of triggering more fissions.

buildup.text: Water is the most common moderator—hydrogen atoms in water are similar in mass to neutrons, ideal for slowing them.

discovery.text: Coolants carry heat away from the reactor core—often the same water serves as both moderator and coolant.

twist.text: Some reactors use heavy water or graphite as moderators—enabling the use of natural (unenriched) uranium.

climax.text: If the coolant is lost, the fuel can overheat and melt—this is a core meltdown, the most feared reactor accident.

punchline.text: Slow the neutron, cool the core—lose either and trouble starts.

quiz.question: What is the primary role of a moderator?
options: Slow neutrons to increase fission probability
